event_confirmation: Company 6-K exhibit 99.1 filed 2026-10-21 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1131383/000117184326006726/exh_991.htm): Q3 2026 results released Thursday 2026-11-12 after market close; webcast/call Friday 2026-11-13 08:00 ET with CEO Susan Reisbord and CFO Vito Culmone. The print is inside the 11-12 close to 11-13 close window.
conviction_note: Balanced evidence: a peer (WSP, 2026-11-04) flagged slower Americas project conversion and the company's own H2 guide needs high-single-digit US organic growth after a flat Q2, set against a margin guide the CFO called conservative, supportive US water read-throughs (Arcadis, Tetra Tech) and a modest, rising short; findings sum to -0.2, p_up 48 on a 4.0% abs move gives -0.16. Both measurements agree in sign and size: there is no edge here beyond noise, and this name has sold its last two EPS beats (Q1 -6.6%, Q2 -0.3%), so the small positive print read does not carry into the reaction.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS consensus US$1.24 (Earnings Whispers preview reproduced on finviz, 2026-11-04, https://finviz.com/news/416299/stantecs-us-rebound-faces-its-first-real-test-as-new-ceo-takes-over) and US$1.26 (Earnings Whispers ticker page, https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/stn); at Q3 USD/CAD of roughly 1.39-1.42 that is about C$1.72-1.79 against C$1.53 a year ago (Q3 2025 6-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1131383/000117184325007292/exh_991.htm), i.e. +12-17%, around the company's FY2026 adjusted EPS growth guide of 15-18% (Q2 2026 6-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001131383/000117184326005457/exh_991.htm). Full-year consensus US$4.43 sits just below the bottom of the USD-translated guide (US$4.46-4.57) per the same preview. The revenue consensus (~US$1.3B, 'implies a 16% decline') is a currency/gross-vs-net artefact and is not usable. The bar is two agreeing aggregator sources in converted currency plus a company growth guide, so it is treated as partially sourced and sizes are kept small.
positioning_check: US-listed (NYSE) short interest 2,583,754 shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, down from 2,612,986 on 10-15 and up from 1,693,804 on 2026-05-29; 7.49 days to cover on NYSE volume only (equibles.com/stocks/stn/shortinterest, read 2026-11-12). Against roughly 114m shares outstanding that is about 2.3%, and most volume trades on the TSX (STN.TO about 400-650k shares a day), so days to cover overall is far lower: not a crowded short, but it has risen about 50% since May. No usable option skew: the baseline chain is unusable (ATM spread 103% of mid, total OI 137), skew_25d null, put/call OI 0.21. Run-up +9.7% over 20 days, -29.7% from the 52-week high; the de-rating is attributed to fears that AI erodes engineering-consultancy fees (Barchart/Globe and Mail coverage), not to results.

findings.finding: WSP Global, Stantec's largest Canadian peer, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-04 after the close with group organic net revenue growth of 5.1%, but said the Americas 'experienced a more measured pace of project conversion' (Americas backlog organic growth 4.9%), and reiterated rather than raised 2026 guidance; WSP.TO fell from C$199.12 to C$181.45 over the next two sessions (-8.9%), and STN fell 3.8% on 11-05 in sympathy (US$78.81 to US$75.81), now US$75.77. This is a read-through that Stantec's US business, flat organic in Q2, may still be slow to convert backlog in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: US organic growth is the line STN has traded on: Q1 2026 (US organic ~2.8%, guide trimmed later) fell -6.6% on 2026-05-14; Q2 2026 (US organic 0%, organic guide trimmed to mid-single digits) moved -0.3% on 2026-08-13 (Yahoo daily closes).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: STN already lost 3.8% the day after WSP and has not recovered that ground (US$75.77 vs US$78.81). What is not priced is whether Stantec's own US number shows the same slow conversion; had the market fully priced a US miss, STN would have kept falling with WSP's second down day (WSP -4.2% on 11-06, STN -1.9%) instead of recovering to flat by 11-12.
findings.independence: Company's own Q2 2026 call says US was flat on delayed starts (Navy environmental program, US West utility, US South transit) and treated it as timing (https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/STN/Q22026). WSP group release also at https://www.wsp.com/en-gl/investors/press-releases/details/WSP-reports-strong-Q3-2026-results-and-backlog-growth/3395916/2026 (403 to fetch; same document as the Archyde copy).

findings.finding: Stantec's own guidance arithmetic sets a high H2 bar: YTD organic net revenue growth is 3.7% (Q1 3.6%, Q2 3.7%) and US organic YTD about 1.4% (Q1 ~2.8%, Q2 0%), yet the reaffirmed outlook calls for mid-single-digit organic growth for the year with the US and Canada reaching mid-single digits; on the Q2 call RBC noted this implies high-single-digit US organic growth in H2. A first quarter under a new CEO (Susan Reisbord from 2026-10-01), with a 2027-2029 strategic plan due in December, is a natural moment to trim the organic guide again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last organic trim (Q2 2026, to mid-single digits from mid-to-high) moved the stock -0.3%, i.e. largely priced at the time; the Q1 2026 print, where the US slowed, fell -6.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Full-year consensus US$4.43 EPS already sits just below the guide's bottom, so the street is leaning to a shortfall on earnings, but the organic revenue guide itself has not been cut; if a second organic trim were expected, the preview coverage would frame it as the base case rather than 'near or slightly short of targets'. Net of the rest: Global (about a third of revenue) is guided to high-single digits and grew 12.8% organic in Q2 (Scottish Water and UK/Australia water), which can carry the consolidated number even if the US lags, so this is sized net of that.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 call transcript (RBC question on implied H2 US high-single-digit growth, management 'Q3 expected to show good organic growth, strengthening in Q4'): https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/STN/Q22026. Shares the company-guidance basis with nothing else in this file; the WSP finding is a separate document.

findings.finding: Margin guide looks conservative: Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin was 18.7% (+90 bps YoY) and YTD expansion about 80 bps, while the raised FY range of 17.8-18.3% implies only about 15 bps more expansion in H2 per the RBC question on the call; CFO Culmone said there is 'some conservatism' in the full-year guide and attributed the H2 moderation to hiring ahead of growth. A Q3 margin at or above the Q2 level would support adjusted EPS above the ~+13% consensus implies and could lift the margin range again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: STN has beaten EPS and been sold: Q1 2026 adjusted EPS +14.7% then -6.6%; Q2 2026 adjusted EPS +18.4% with margin range raised then -0.3%; Q4 2025 appears to have risen about +5.5% (US$90.27 to US$95.23 on 2026-02-26) on results and 2026 guidance. Margin beats alone have not paid.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus Q3 EPS of US$1.24-1.26 converts to roughly +12-17% YoY, inside the 15-18% FY guide, so a margin-driven beat lands inside what the company told the market to expect; that is why it is sized small. If the market priced a margin beat, consensus would sit at the top of the growth guide rather than the FY number just below its bottom.
findings.independence: WSP's Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 20.5% on 'strong margins in the US and Canada' (https://www.archyde.com/wsp-reports-strong-q3-2026-results-with-record-order-backlog/), a peer confirming margin strength in the same geographies. Q2 6-K margin figures: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001131383/000117184326005457/exh_991.htm

findings.finding: Tetra Tech (direct US water/environmental peer) reported its fiscal Q4 (to 2026-09-27) on 2026-11-11 after the close: net revenue about US$1.15B, inside its own guide, +5% excluding disaster response, backlog +13% YoY to US$4.67B, and FY2027 net revenue guide of US$4.425-4.625B (about +4% at the midpoint); its government-segment net revenue fell about 5% while commercial/international rose about 3%. TTEK fell 7.5% on 11-11 before the release and rose 4.4% on 11-12 after it; STN was flat both days.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history of STN reacting to TTEK prints in the sources read.
findings.why_not_priced: Released the night before STN's print; STN did not move on 11-12 (US$75.50 to 75.77), so the read-through is not visibly in the price either way. The read is mixed: US water and backlog strong, US government softer, which matters for Stantec's delayed Navy environmental program. Proxy only.
findings.independence: TTEK price closes from Yahoo chart (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/TTEK?range=1mo&interval=1d). Arcadis finding below is a separate peer with a similar US water read.

findings.finding: Arcadis Q3 2026 trading update (2026-10-28): group organic net revenue growth accelerated to 4.3%, backlog organic +7.9%, 'US Water revenues increasing double digit year-on-year', 2026 guide reaffirmed. Stantec's water business was already growing above 20% and is the US unit's strongest line; this supports the water piece of the US H2 ramp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history of STN reacting to Arcadis.
findings.why_not_priced: Two weeks old and public, so largely priced; filed small as a peer confirmation that US water demand held through Q3. Net of the rest: water is only part of the US unit; the delayed utility, transit and Navy work is the swing.
findings.independence: Tetra Tech's release says demand for its water and environmental services is increasing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000831641/000110465926125600/tm2629545d1_ex99-1.htm).

findings.finding: The IIJA surface transportation authorities were extended only to 2026-12-11, and the extension did not carry the IIJA's Division J advance appropriations, which NACo estimated cuts overall highway funding by more than 15% from 2026-10-01. Management commentary on the Q3 call about US transportation award flow into Q4 and 2027 could be cautious.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the sources; the Q2 call raised the related risk of the new-award window closing, without a measured price reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro and public since September; filed small because the company has not said how much of its US backlog depends on Division J money, and design work on awarded projects continues. A clear pricing of this risk would show up in STN lagging US-only peers after October 1, which it has not (it rose about 10% over 20 days).
findings.independence: NACo on the Division J omission: https://www.naco.org/news/senate-funding-proposal-would-create-transportation-funding-cliff-counties. Proxy, macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by the company.

findings.finding: USD/CAD traded around 1.39-1.42 through Q3 2026, against the 1.38 assumed in Stantec's 2026 outlook and about 1.38 a year earlier, a small translation tailwind for CAD-reported net revenue and EPS from the roughly half of revenue earned in the US.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts who model in CAD will have most of it; it matters for whether reported numbers land at the top of a CAD-denominated guide. Small by construction.
findings.independence: Guidance FX assumption USD 1.38 in the Q2 6-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001131383/000117184326005457/exh_991.htm

findings.finding: Stantec repurchased 1,667,292 shares for C$175.9m (about C$105.5 a share) in H1 2026 and raised its NCIB limit to 5% from 2% in August; STN.TO trades at about C$108 now, near where it bought. Q3 buyback volume and any statement about using the larger authorisation are capital-return items the call can update.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 2026 NCIB expansion came with a flat stock (-0.3% on the Q2 print).
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation is public; the Q3 execution is not. Preview coverage lists buyback progress as something investors are watching, which suggests the amount is not yet known.

outside_window.finding: Stantec's 2027-2029 strategic plan is due in December 2026 (per the Q2 call); targets there could reset the multiple either way, but the investor event is after the window (the Q3 call may only preview it).
The IIJA authorisation extension expires 2026-12-11; a further extension or a long-term bill (BUILD America 250 Act) would resolve the US transportation-funding question after the window.

baseline_tension: No usable skew or implied move to agree or disagree with; the evidence is two-sided and roughly offsetting, consistent with a stock that has already de-rated 30% and bounced about 10% in 20 days.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name has sold its last two EPS beats): margin-conservatism finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3; it also lands inside the guided EPS growth range (rule 6).
Rule 9 (size a segment finding net of the rest): H2 US/organic-gap finding cut from -0.7 to -0.6 because Global (about a third of revenue, 12.8% organic in Q2) can carry the consolidated number.
Rule 5 (proxy small): Arcadis cut from +0.3 to +0.2, IIJA Division J from -0.3 to -0.2; WSP read-through cut from -0.8 to -0.7 because STN already fell 3.8% on it.
Last lesson (reaction history from wrong events): the baseline's 6-K history was rebuilt from confirmed releases before sizing abs_move_pct; abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged at 4.0 and 48.
